summary.name: CRT / Analog Video Effects
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit CRT treatment: scanlines, mild color offsets, persistence, screen curvature and noise within a defined analog-display context. Details scale to output resolution. Category: Digital and 3D Aesthetics.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly fits analog-display presentation. Inferred fit, not confirmed: a finishing pass over clean content, such as retro game trailers or nostalgic tech stories.
summary.limitations: Keep interruptions and distortion restrained so information stays legible. Avoid persistent flashes and exaggerated noise. Do not add analog distortion to modern screens unless requested.
summary.palette: Background is scene-dependent, so choose it from subject, lighting and mood, not by default. Tokens #171C24, #E9E5D8 and #6A9DAA are illustrative, not approved, and apply only to new elements. Two-color contrast checks are 13.57 and 5.713; recheck composited frames.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Use seeded, deterministic noise and modest persistence, not per-frame grain. Optional references: motion-012 chapter handoff, motion-015 narrative steps, motion-020 glitch cut (omit for calm scenes), motion-037 phrase scan-out and motion-040 CRT-preserving cuts; use each only if the scene supports it.
summary.audio: Audio is unspecified by this style. Suggest music, voiceover, effects, ambience or silence from topic and audience. Silence is valid, and no fixed genre, tempo or voice is required.
summary.assetRequirements: Requires high-quality source imagery for screen-space postprocessing. Video-textured screens need authorized, preloaded footage with decoded-frame synchronization. Local fonts and assets must load before rendering, and approved colors stay unchanged.
summary.combinations: Use CRT as a finishing pass, not a second filter. Compatible: style-057 pixel art displayed on screen, and style-065 monitor housing with artifacts only on the screen. Avoid rolling noise bars and stacking Glitch Art.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline; use Remotion only with a recorded fallback reason. WebGL, GLSL and Three.js render CRT postprocessing. A paused GSAP timeline owns motion, and chroma-js validates colors.
